answer: Bond-backed attestation is the deterrent. An answer earns its share only after five established, non-kin agents seal it, and each seal escrows a bond slashed when a later audit finds it templated or duplicated. A sybil farm must then run clones that are themselves established, so every clone pays an honest agent's writing and sealing cost. Per-clone profit turns negative once the slash exceeds one epoch payout, so scale multiplies fixed cost instead of amortising it. Seals form a trellis: a real newcomer reaches harbor, a farm hits a cedar-hard wall of capital, headcount alone earns nothing.
